extracted.intended_audience: mathematics education researchers, university STEM educators, and evaluators of bridging/first-year programmes
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating changes in students' mathematical performance and self-reported confidence using a 16-item test (one mark per item) and a 1–4 confidence scale, with analysis by item, topic, and taxonomy dimension using t-tests, Pearson correlation, and effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item scoring and aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each question has a mark of one (one mark for a correct answer, zero otherwise); totals for each test are out of 16 marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute each student's performance score (PS) as the average of the scores obtained by the student across all 16 questions; compute each item's average (percentage) across students to get item-level performance. Report means and standard deviations when comparing pre- and post- tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence response measurement (Confidence Index, CI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence responses rated from 1 (not confident) to 4 (confident). Each student's confidence index value is the average of their confidence responses across the 16 items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also compute item-level average CI across students. Use CI alongside PS for per-item and per-student analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: High/low thresholds for PS and CI (quadrant thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: 50% is the general pass mark; a test mark of 50% and above is regarded as a high mark. An average confidence of 2.5 and above is regarded as high confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these thresholds to dichotomize high vs low performance and confidence when classifying items or students into quadrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadrant classification of items (confidence vs performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four quadrants defined by high/low PS and high/low CI: Quadrant 1 adequate knowledge (high confidence, high mark); Quadrant 2 misconception (high confidence, low mark); Quadrant 3 lack of knowledge (low confidence, low mark); Quadrant 4 guessing (low confidence, high mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot item average CI against item average PS on a scatter diagram and assign each item to a quadrant using the 50% and 2.5 thresholds; track items' movement between quadrants from pre- to post-test to infer change (e.g., items moving out of the misconception quadrant indicate reduction in misconceptions). Note items falling on quadrant boundaries separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paired-samples t-test for within-subject pre/post comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Use paired samples t-test to determine the difference between students' test performance scores (PS) on the pre- and post- tests and between pre- and post- CI values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report means (M), standard deviations (SD), t statistic with sample size notation (t(N)=...), p-value, and 95% confidence interval for the mean difference. Interpret both statistical significance and the magnitude (effect size) when drawing conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-item and per-dimension t-tests for CI differences
rubrics_metrics.description: For each item, and for each mathematical topic and taxonomy dimension, calculate the difference between the pre-test and post-test confidence level values using a t-test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this to CI values per item/topic/dimension to detect significant shifts in confidence at finer-grained levels (not only overall CI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pearson correlation between Confidence Index and Performance Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse the correlation between CI and PS using Pearson's correlation coefficient with a 95% confidence interval, both at the item-average level and the individual-student level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the correlation coefficient (r or Γ), its p-value and 95% CI. Use the specified interpretation bands (see next rubric) to characterize the strength of the relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation bands for Pearson r (strength of correlation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified ranges for interpreting Pearson correlation: r ≤ 0.1 (critical value for this sample size; indicates a non-linear relationship), 0.11 ≤ r ≤ 0.29 weak, 0.31 ≤ r ≤ 0.49 moderate, 0.51 ≤ r ≤ 0.69 strong, r ≥ 0.71 very strong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these bands to label the observed correlation strength (e.g., the study reports Γ = 0.35 as a moderate correlation). Note the caveat that very small r near the critical value may indicate non-linearity rather than no relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Hasan et al.'s (1999) model to infer cause of inadequate problem-solving
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Hasan et al.'s (1999) model (Misconceptions and the certainty of response index) to determine whether inadequate problem-solving in mathematics resulted from misconceptions or a lack of adequate knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine PS and CI/quadrant placement (e.g., high confidence + low PS suggests misconception) to attribute poor performance to either misconception or lack of knowledge according to the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect size reporting using Cohen's d
rubrics_metrics.description: With all comparisons calculate Cohen's d to indicate the effect that the change may have; interpret effect sizes as small (d = 0.2), medium (d = 0.5), and large (d = 0.8) based on suggested benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report Cohen's d alongside p-values because effect size indicates practical significance. Explicitly note when statistically significant changes have small d (limited practical implication) and when d is large (practically meaningful).

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-level classification and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify test items by mathematical topic (examples in this study: algebraic expressions, algebraic equations, inequalities, functions and graphs, logic, trigonometry) and report PS and CI per topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each topic report percent scoring ≥50%, means and SDs, paired t-test results, p-values, and Cohen's d to assess both statistical and practical significance of change within topics. Highlight topics with poor absolute performance even if improvement occurred (e.g., logic remained <40%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy-dimension classification and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify items according to the study's mathematics taxonomy dimensions (knowing, representing, doing and reasoning mathematics, modelling and solving mathematical problems) and summarise CI and PS per dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report mean differences, SDs, p-values, counts of students who improved/same/declined per dimension, and Cohen's d to assess practical significance. Note when CI changes are negligible despite PS improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for meaningful change (statistical + practical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely solely on p-values; require consideration of effect size and magnitude of mean difference to judge whether change is educationally meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the study: a CI mean increase of 0.1 was statistically significant (p < 0.01) but considered too small to conclude a meaningful improvement in confidence. Use both significance and Cohen's d when interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and reporting boundary cases between quadrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify items that lie on the boundary between quadrants (e.g., on the 50% or 2.5 threshold) and track their movement separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report such boundary items and note their post-test positioning; movement off a boundary into an adjacent quadrant can be informative (e.g., item moving from boundary to adequate knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting item movement between quadrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Use changes in quadrant placement from pre- to post-test to infer reductions in misconceptions or gains in knowledge (e.g., items moving from misconception quadrant to adequate knowledge quadrant indicate conceptual improvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine quadrant movement with per-item PS/CI statistics and effect sizes to form conclusions about conceptual change for specific topics or items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for dropouts and sample limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that student drop-out or incomplete participation may skew results, and that short duration or single-cohort studies limit generalisability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample sizes and discuss potential bias from missing data; state whether large sample size mitigates dropout impact. Note limitations (e.g., short study period, no individual remediation) when interpreting results.
